premise: I gave my stepdaughter $88,000 from my late husband’s pension to complete her cosmetology school and open her own salon with a contract stating I’d receive 30% of profits until my death; she opened a high-end salon, sold it for $950,000 two years later, forged a release of my interest, and paid me $10,000 as a ‘thank you.’ I uncovered the forgery, sued for breach of contract and fraud, and was awarded $260,000 — when she couldn’t pay, I obtained a garnishment order against her new yoga studio, which I then purchased at a sheriff’s sale; now I operate ‘Yoga & Lipstick’ with a wall of shame displaying her forged document, and she’s forced to teach a free weekly class called ‘Flexing the Truth.’
